task: Fix the event deduplication failure after the event ID format changed.

candidate_memories.content: Duplicate events are being processed because the deduplication check uses the old integer ID format but new events use UUID format.
The deduplication key must be updated to use the UUID event ID; the old integer check always misses UUID-keyed events.
The event ID format changed in version 4.3.0 deployed on April 7; events before that date have integer IDs.
When event ID formats change, update all deduplication, routing, and storage components in the same release.
Historical events with integer IDs are not being duplicated; only new events with UUID IDs are affected.
The event streaming platform was migrated from Kafka to Kinesis in Q2.
Session 9 note: the event schema was extended with a new metadata field for trace IDs.
Old lesson: integer IDs were used for events before UUIDs were adopted for global uniqueness.
Events are retained in Kinesis for 7 days; historical events older than 7 days are in S3.
A data consistency check in session 5 showed no duplicates for events before version 4.3.0.
Old event guide: deduplication was handled by the downstream consumer, not the event broker.
When event IDs change format, run a dual-write compatibility period before switching deduplication logic.
Session 12 note: the event replay feature was added for audit log reconstruction.
The analytics pipeline processes events in micro-batches of 500 per 10 seconds.
Session 7 note: the monitoring team added alerting for high event processing latency.
Event consumers are deployed as Kubernetes Deployments with horizontal autoscaling.
Deduplication windows should exceed the maximum expected event redelivery delay.
Session 3 note: the event schema versioning policy was documented in the architecture decision record.
Old deduplication guide: the deduplication window was 24 hours for integer IDs; it was reduced to 1 hour.
Event producers include both the web app and the mobile app SDKs.
